For Couples: Forest River Shows Off They Can Be a Serious RV Brand With 2027 Pause Reboot 14.3
15 photos
Photo: Forest River Inc
Usually, when you do out there and lock your eyes onto a compact travel trailer, you expect to also come across an equally ‘compact’ price. Well, when we’re talking about Forest River’s Pause Reboot 14.3, the idea that a smaller camper is accompanied by a small price goes out the window.
That’s because, for the time being, a 2027 Pause Reboot 14.3 is currently selling in select dealerships for an average of $75,000, a price that usually lands you in a massive travel trailer suitable for an entire family, and not just a traveling couple. Why is that? That’s what we’re here to find out.
If you’ve ever followed along with content revolving around this camper , you’re aware that this one is nothing like your average travel trailer of this size. Since it was launched in 2024, people have even come to love the Pause Reboot class for its ability to be a dependable solution for off-grid camping.
Photo: Forest River Inc Now, there are countless ways to build a camper, and at the core of the 14.3, Forest River ditched the wood and calls upon a completely composite and aluminum-framed design. This means a camper that’s as impervious to the elements as possible and one that is also as light as can be.
The latter is relative to just how capable a camper may be, and in the case of the 14.3, keep in mind that it weighs 4,583 lbs (2,079 kg). Quite the hefty bugger for a camper that is just shy of 18 feet (5.5 m) and stands at a bit over 10.5 ft (3.2 m) tall.
One reason for the weight has a whole lot to do with the running gear underneath this camper, a setup that is independent one with a shear spring setup of around 5 inches of travel and even tested in Moab; it’s completed by MoRyde. According to sources, the reason for shear springs as opposed to airbags or traditional springs has to do with keeping the weight down as much as possible.
Photo: Forest River Inc This wheel action also means that we can easily break away from the tarmac and gravel roads and really venture deep into the wild, but it also means less stress on your camper’s shell, helping prolong its life, and some current camper owners do purchase and used preloved Pause Reboot trailers and are more than happy with the state they’re in.
Aside from the suspension, people also rave about the wood-free construction, standing up to the elements year after year. Just keep in mind that maintenance and upkeep is a must, even for a camper of this sort of construction.
As for the living experience we can tap into once we’ve reached our hidden haven, owners really enjoy the features that Forest River includes in the unit, mentioning that "it has everything we could need and ask for, and nothing extra we don’t use.”
Photo: Forest River Inc Features like the outdoor kitchen and cooler are among the loved ones, and so is the side-mounted table located near the rear, but inside, is really where Forest River shows off that they too can craft a camper worth the bucks; typically, this brand has a bad wrap when it comes to campers, but the Pause Reboot lineup does seem to “reboot” our confidence in the brand. It’s as if Forest River either makes campers people hate or love.
The interior of the 14.3 surprised me in the fact that it includes yet another complete kitchen, this time with standing fridge, a dining area that can be transformed into an extra bed for a child, a matrimonial bed for two, and even a dry bath. Yes, the toilet sits separate the shower but there is no vanity.
This is a trait that we rarely see in a camper of this size, but as I mentioned, Forest River really went all out on this lineup.
Photo: Forest River Inc Storage is clearly not a problem for the 14.3 either, with the interior displaying ample options for your gear and personal belongings, but outside we also find a neat little platform at the rear of the camper that allows us to put down a couple of e-bikes, climbing and fishing gear, and whatever else you can secure to the space; it can handle 300 lbs. A spare tire is also usually found mounted to this tray. The GVWR of the 14.3 stands at 5,868 lbs (2,662 kgs).
While there is a large nose-cone box mounted in the 14.3’s frame, it’s onto more important traits of this unit, like the off-grid features and systems that are in place as standard. None other than Victron is called upon to handle our power needs and instead of boring you with a long list of systems, inverters, and batteries, I invite you to check out the clip on a 2026 14.3 below to see what’s in store.
Photo: Forest River Inc Keep in mind that off-grid capabilities are expandable, and we can tap into 800 W of solar and 1,296 Ah of lithium. When’s the last time you heard of a Forest River with this much kick?
Frankly, it’s these reasons and a few others that force the Pause Reboot 14.3 to carry such a high price tag, and while Forest River isn’t always the first choice for Americans, in the past year or so, I have been seeing some changes in the brand, with units that seem to be designed and built with a bit more attention than, let’s say, five years ago.
Would you rock a Pause Reboot 14.3? Drop your comments below.
